lessons.title: Story Time: The Minibeast Hunt
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to make predictions about a minibeast-themed story.
success_criteria: I can predict what minibeast will be found.
I can check my prediction.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a minibeast-hunt-themed story, modelling prediction.
lessons.independent_task: Children record predictions and check them against the story.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note prediction skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Go on a mini minibeast hunt with your family.

lessons.title: Counting Minibeast Legs
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count in steps to solve a minibeast-themed problem.
success_criteria: I can count in steps of 6 or 8.
I can find a total number of legs.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting minibeast legs (insects have 6, spiders have 8) using repeated addition/counting in steps.
lessons.independent_task: Children count total legs for groups of minibeasts, recording their working.
key_questions: How did you work it out?

differentiation.support: Count legs for 2-3 minibeasts with support
differentiation.greater_depth: Count legs for 5+ minibeasts and find grand totals

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of counting in steps to a real problem — evidence for MATHS.N1/N3.
lessons.home_link: Count the legs of any minibeasts you find.

lessons.title: What Is a Microhabitat?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe what a microhabitat is.
success_criteria: I can define a microhabitat.
I can name an example.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss small places minibeasts might live (under a log, in a crack).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the concept of a microhabitat as a small specific habitat within a larger one.
lessons.independent_task: Children identify examples of microhabitats from pictures, recording what lives there.

differentiation.greater_depth: Identify 5+ examples and predict creatures for each

lessons.assessment_notes: Note microhabitat concept understanding — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Look for a microhabitat in your garden (under a stone, in leaf litter).

lessons.title: Drawing Minibeasts in Detail
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to draw a minibeast with observational detail.
success_criteria: I can draw the correct number of legs.
I can add pattern/texture detail.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model observational drawing of a minibeast, counting legs and noting patterns.
lessons.independent_task: Children draw a chosen minibeast with observational detail.
key_questions: How many legs does your minibeast have?

differentiation.greater_depth: Add fine detail and accurate proportions

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe observational drawing skill and scientific accuracy — evidence for ART.1/SCI.LIV.

lessons.title: Writing a Minibeast Fact File
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write a simple non-fiction fact file about a minibeast.
success_criteria: I can write 2-3 facts about a minibeast.
I can organise facts under headings.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a fact file with simple headings (appearance, habitat, food).
lessons.independent_task: Children write their own minibeast fact file with headings.

differentiation.greater_depth: Add extra headings and detail independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction organisational writing skill — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family 3 facts from your fact file.

lessons.title: Symmetry in Minibeasts
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify symmetry in minibeast bodies.
success_criteria: I can say if a minibeast is symmetrical.
I can draw a symmetrical minibeast.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model identifying symmetry in minibeast pictures (ladybird, butterfly) and drawing a symmetrical minibeast using the fold technique.
lessons.independent_task: Children create a symmetrical minibeast using the paint-blot fold technique.
key_questions: How did you make yours symmetrical?

differentiation.greater_depth: Create a more detailed symmetrical design

lessons.assessment_notes: Note symmetry understanding and application — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.home_link: Look for symmetry in minibeasts or nature at home.

lessons.title: Exploring a Microhabitat
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explore and record findings from a real microhabitat.
success_criteria: I can carefully explore a microhabitat.
I can record what I find.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap being gentle and careful when exploring nature.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model carefully lifting a log/stone (or using a provided resource) to explore a microhabitat, recording findings.
lessons.independent_task: Children explore a real or simulated microhabitat, recording what they find (or observe via photos/video if outdoor access isn't possible).
resources_needed: Access to an outdoor microhabitat, or photo/video resources
lessons.assessment_notes: Note fieldwork and observational skill, a key working scientifically objective — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Carefully explore a microhabitat at home with an adult.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Minibeast Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read minibeast-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read minibeast words.
I can read a sentence about minibeasts.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to minibeast-themed words (e.g. 'spider', 'beetle', 'worm').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading minibeast words over the week.

lessons.title: Minibeast Survey: Block Diagram
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct a simple block diagram of survey data.
success_criteria: I can build a block diagram.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the minibeast hunt data from Monday's home link.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model constructing a block diagram of minibeasts found/known, one block per creature.
lessons.independent_task: Children build a block diagram from minibeast survey data and answer questions about it.
key_questions: How many more of this than that?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record introduction of block diagrams, a Year 2 statistics objective — evidence for MATHS.STAT.
lessons.home_link: Make a simple block diagram of something at home.

lessons.title: Minibeast Adaptations
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how a minibeast is suited to its microhabitat.
success_criteria: I can name a minibeast adaptation.
I can say how it helps.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss why a woodlouse might curl into a ball.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss minibeast adaptations (camouflage, hard shells, curling up) and how they help survival.
lessons.independent_task: Children match minibeasts to their adaptations, recording reasoning.
key_questions: How does this adaptation help the minibeast?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of adaptation to microhabitat — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Talk about how a minibeast you've seen might be adapted to survive.

lessons.title: Presenting Our Minibeast Fact Files
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present a minibeast fact file clearly to the class.
success_criteria: I can share a fact about my minibeast.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap fact files written on Tuesday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear presentation of a fact file.
lessons.independent_task: Children present their minibeast fact file to a small group, answering a question.
key_questions: Can you answer a question about your minibeast?

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and non-fiction knowledge presentation — evidence for ENG.SL1/SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Present your minibeast fact file to your family.

lessons.title: Minibeast Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using a minibeast context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using a minibeast context (e.g. woodlice found under logs).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve minibeast-themed word problems within 100, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a minibeast word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Being Gentle with Minibeasts
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how to handle and observe minibeasts safely and gently.
success_criteria: I can name a rule for being gentle with minibeasts.
I can say why it matters.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss why we should be careful with small creatures.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss safe, gentle minibeast handling and observation (look, don't squeeze; return to habitat).
lessons.independent_task: Children create a 'Minibeast Explorer Rules' poster.
key_questions: Why should we be gentle with minibeasts?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning into environmental responsibility — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.home_link: Talk about being gentle with small creatures at home.

lessons.title: Microhabitats and Minibeasts Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about microhabitats and minibeasts.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about microhabitats and minibeasts, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why does a woodlouse curl into a ball?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on minibeast facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Symmetry and Data
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply symmetry and data handling skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can identify symmetry.
I can read a block diagram.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of symmetry and block diagrams.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: symmetry, data handling.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 6 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.GEO/STAT.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue looking for symmetry over the weekend.

lessons.title: Microhabitats and Minibeasts Topic Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about microhabitats and minibeasts.
success_criteria: I can name a microhabitat and a minibeast found there.
I can name an adaptation.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering microhabitats, minibeasts, and adaptations.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Microhabitats and Minibeasts' display featuring their fact files and drawings.
key_questions: What have we learned about microhabitats?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note microhabitat and adaptation understanding progress, setting up food chains next week — evidence for SCI.LIV.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate the week's microhabitats and minibeasts learning.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about minibeasts with your family.
